Former anchor of ABC's World News Now and America This Morning, Paula delivered unforgettable and colorful accounts from the World Cup. As the audience on the weekend continues to grow, GMA is now the #1 morning newscast on Saturdays and regularly beats NBC's Today on Sunday mornings.

name: Episode 59
summary:
7am: Thousands of Americans took to the streets to protest against ICE and the Trump administration's harsh immigration crackdown. The demonstrations come as Trump is urging ICE to keep up aggressive traffic-stop operations despite the recent deadly shootings. At the same time, Trump spent this week focused on reviving election conspiracy theories, laying out the groundwork to challenge midterm election results if Republicans lose. President of Media Matters, Angelo Carusone, joins "The Weekend" to discuss.

8am: But across the country, voters have more real-world concerns. With that in mind, Democrats are trying to win over voters, even in red states like Iowa, by focusing on the future and practical concerns. Former Transportation Sec. Pete Buttigieg was in the Hawkeye State and Florida this week holding events with Democratic candidates running for office there. He joined The Weekend to weighs in on the path forward for Democrats as we move ever-closer to the midterm elections.

9am: More than two dozen House Democrats met this week for a closed-door strategy session to map out how they would respond if President Trump tried to interfere in this year's midterms. House Democrats have told MS NOW that one fear they have is that Trump could be using the Save America Act as a pretext, and if the legislation fails, Trump could declare a state of emergency to make electoral rule changes. Congressman Joe Morelle of New York, who organized the meeting with House Democrats, joins "The Weekend" along with Skye Perryman, President and CEO of Democracy Forward.

show.name: Fareed Zakaria GPS
show.summary: Fareed Zakaria GPS is a weekly public affairs show hosted by journalist and author Fareed Zakaria. As of November 2011, the show airs Sundays at 10 am Eastern Time and 1 pm Eastern Time on CNN. The show also airs Sundays at 1200 and 1900 GMT on CNN International. The "GPS" in the show's title stands for "Global Public Square," a reference to the show's focus on international issues and foreign affairs. On August 10, 2012, CNN suspended the program pending their investigation of suspected plagiarism. One week later, the New York Times reported, "Time and CNN said they had completed their reviews, found no evidence of plagiarism, and restored Mr. Zakaria to his demanding schedule." Each installment features Zakaria leading a panel discussion and conducting an extended one-on-one interview.

summary:
President Trump is undermining American elections again, this time with a team of loyalists and without guardrails. Ellen Weintraub, whom Trump fired without cause from the FEC, explains why this is cause for alarm; David Rohde provides updates on two American servicemembers killed in Jordan and Trump's election task force; Victoria Eavis details new reporting of a massive ICE sweep in Montana that captured hospitality staff for the Yellowstone Club, a hub for the ultra-wealthy; Jacob reads viewer social media posts in this week's "Ask Me Anything."

United Nations Special Rapporteur Margaret Satterthwaite explains how the termination of dozens of immigration judges by the Trump administration has undermined America's democracy; California Polytechnic State University student Tobias Halpern explains why he fought to get Flock cameras off his college campus and journalist Adrian Carrasquillo uncovers why those cameras are raising serious privacy concerns; Chef Moe explains how to make meals out of $5 and how he gained a massive following on social media by sharing that information with the public  

After President Trump's election fraud speech, threats have started to roll in against election workers. show.name: Snapped
show.summary: Who are these women and what drives them to kill? Oxygen's hit true crime series, Snapped, profiles fascinating cases of women accused of murder. Did they really do it? And if they did, why? Whether the motivation is revenge against a cheating husband, the promise of a hefty insurance payoff, or putting an end to years of abuse, the reasons are as varied as the women themselves. From socialites to secretaries, female killers share one thing in common: at some point, they all snapped. Each episode of Snapped chronicles the life of a woman who has been charged with murder. These shocking but true stories turn common assumptions about crime and criminals upside down, and prove that even the most unlikely suspects can be capable of murder.

name: Adam Holbrook: Elvis Presley
summary: Elvis Presley may be the King of Rock 'n' Roll, but Adam Holbrook just might be the king of collecting all things Elvis. After a lifetime of gathering treasures and more than 50 trips to Graceland, Adam and his partner, Mari Guerrero, now share their finds on their popular YouTube channel, and today, they're sharing them with Lisa and general appraiser Kate Martin. Together, they shake, rattle, and roll through Elvis history, from the King's own guitar pick, to a quirky array of Presley-branded grooming items, and even the floor vent salvaged from Colonel Tom Parker's home. Kate appraises Adam and Mari's collection before proposing a trade – unveiling a pristine vintage Presley travel case in hopes it's enough to convince them to let a beloved Elvis item leave the building.

name: Jul 19 Sun
summary: After the U.S. vowed to punish Iran for killing two U.S. forces in Jordan, another service member has been killed in action in northern Iraq. Officials say they have also recovered unidentified remains at the site of a deadly attack in Jordan where U.S. service members were killed. NBC News' Keir Simmons has the latest. Parts of the Southeast could see wind gusts reach 70 mph, putting millions of Americans under severe weather threat. Meanwhile cleanup is underway in the Northeast after powerful storms pummeled the region, with tornadoes touching down in Pennsylvania. And Canadian wildfire smoke continues to blanket parts of the Midwest with Minneapolis, Detroit and Chicago ranking amongst the worst air quality in the world. NBC News' Valerie Castro reports. The FBI will no longer investigate assault confrontations with ICE agents, according to two people familiar with the directives. According to those sources, FBI special agents in charge of field offices and agents in those field offices were told Thursday that the FBI would no longer investigate cases of assault against a federal officer. NBC News' Julie Tsirkin reports. Taylor Farms expanded their recall of iceberg lettuce to 27 states over concerns they may contain cyclospora, a parasite that causes severe stomach illness. The FDA says the parasite was detected in a sample of lettuce that was not a part of an original recall for five states. NBC News' Priscilla Thompson has the latest. Police are searching for a group of individuals who gained entry to Eagles running back Saquon's Barkley's home early Saturday morning. Authorities say Barkley and his family were home at the time of the invasion but were not harmed. NBC News' Morgan Chesky reports. NBC News' Hallie Jackson sat down with Burger King President Tom Curtis to discuss how his company, famous for its Whopper burgers, is positioning itself at a time when more and more Americans turn to GLP-1s to lose weight.

show.name: NBC Nightly News
show.summary: NBC Nightly News is the most-watched evening newscast in America, providing the very latest on the day's top stories and going beyond the headlines to add context and analysis to the most pressing issues of our time, both at home and abroad. We go to the heart of breaking news stories, introduce you to everyday people caught up in extraordinary events, offer in-depth reporting on health and medicine, cover international news as it unfolds and we profile those who inspire us to do better in our popular Making A Difference reports. The award-winning broadcast carries a legacy that spans more than six decades, beginning in 1948 - when NBC started broadcasting television's first-ever regularly scheduled network evening newscast.

name: Episode 196
summary: New details about standoff in alleged kidnapping of 2 forest service employees. Audio has been released of the incident where authorities say the men were zip-tied and held hostage at gunpoint in a trailer for more than 12 hours before being rescued. ABC News' Jaclyn Lee reports. Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested in Miami after British authorities issued dozens of new charges against them, including allegations of rape and sex trafficking. They denied the allegations. ABC News' Marcus Moore reports. Authorities say NFL star Saquon Barkley was at home with his family in Philadelphia on Saturday morning when they were targeted. ABC News' Perry Russom reports. 2nd Legionnaires' disease death tied to outbreak in New York City. At least 72 people have become sick, and 9 are still hospitalized. Cooling towers on nearly 80 buildings have tested positive for the bacteria that causes Legionnaires' disease. Police: 4 teens under arrest in connection with string of violent crimes in Portland. Police say the arrests of the teens, aged 15 to 17, came after a robbery and shooting at a gas station on Friday. Mass shooting in Tucson, Arizona. Police say a suspect fired randomly into a crowd in a downtown district at around 2 a.m., striking nine people. An officer shot the suspect as he ran away. The couples must marry before their visas expire in 90 days, or the visiting partner will have to return home. They'll have to overcome language barriers, culture shock and skeptical friends and family -- all with a clock that starts ticking the moment they step foot on U.S. soil. The stakes are incredibly high as these couples are forced to make a life-altering decision: get married or send their international mate home.

show.summary: The Maine Cabin Masters take on their most ambitious build yet: transforming a rundown B&B into a stunning 12-acre lakeside inn. Along the way, Chase and his wife, Sarah, bring their long-held dream of becoming innkeepers to life.

show.name: Sunday Night in America with Trey Gowdy
show.summary: Trey Gowdy will offer insightful analysis and a new outlook on the latest issues facing the country. Capitalizing on his experiences as a former prosecutor and Chairman of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, the former South Carolina Congressman will utilize his signature mixture of wisdom, humor and historical references to break down the latest legal and political news from across the nation. "Sunday Night in America" will offer seasoned perspective while providing viewers with the tools and information to draw their own conclusions. The program will also feature timely, solution-oriented interviews with decision makers and Washington insiders, as well as original stories of triumph and success highlighting why Americans should be optimistic about the future.

show.name: Sunday Night in America with Trey Gowdy

show.name: WWE LFG
show.summary: WWE LFG (Legends & Future Greats) will offer viewers an inside look at the rigorous training process, featuring iconic WWE Legends such as Paul "Triple H" Levesque and Shawn Michaels and weekly regular coaches Undertaker, Booker T, Mickie James and Bubba Ray Dudley as they mentor a new generation in weekly matches on their quest to become the next WWE Superstars.

name: Cereal Sensations
summary: Through happy accidents and breakthrough flavor innovations, cereal pioneers battle for control of America's breakfast table-using iconic mascots, unforgettable commercials, and bold new ideas to build a billion-dollar industry.

show.name: The Food That Built America
show.summary: For generations of Americans, food titans like Henry Heinz, Milton Hershey, John and Will Kellogg, C.W. Post and the McDonald brothers have literally been household names, but you don't know their stories. Before they were brand names, they were brilliant, sometimes ruthless, visionaries who revolutionized food and changed the landscape of America forever. This miniseries event will tell the fascinating stories of the people behind the food that built America – those who used brains, muscle, blood, sweat and tears to get to America's heart through its stomach, and along the way built cities, invented new technologies and helped win wars.

show.summary: In the Eye of the Storm Megastorms like 2021's Hurricane Ida and the 2023 Maui Wildfires were captured by onlookers who found themselves in the wrong place at the right time and boldly held up their camera phones to document their experiences.
